question: Should OpenClaw add a generic action-aware tool-policy contract for multiplexed tools, and what trusted bypass semantics should approved workflows use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines a new public config grammar and authorization boundary across message, gateway, sender, sandbox, plugin, and HTTP invocation paths.

options.title: Design Generic Action Policy
options.body: Add a typed action-aware policy grammar enforced before multiplexed tool actions execute, with documented precedence and trusted-context tests for message and gateway.

options.title: Narrow To Known Tools
options.body: Add separate controls only for current message and gateway cases, reducing immediate scope but creating parallel policy surfaces that may drift.

options.title: Defer To Confirmation Work
options.body: Use adjacent confirmation or capability-grant work for human approval and accept that static least-privilege action deny remains unavailable for now.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Action Policy
recommendation.body: Add a typed action-aware policy grammar enforced before multiplexed tool actions execute, with documented precedence and trusted-context tests for message and gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the current issue review and strongest current-history ownership across the implicated config, policy, and message surfaces.
